Package neqsim.thermo.system

Class SystemPitzer

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.system.SystemThermo
neqsim.thermo.system.SystemEos
neqsim.thermo.system.SystemEosGE
neqsim.thermo.system.SystemPitzer
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Cloneable, EosGeFlashModel, HybridEosGeFlashModel, SystemInterface
public class SystemPitzer extends SystemEosGE
Thermodynamic system using the Pitzer GE model for the aqueous phase and SRK EOS for gas and optional oil phases.

Supports vapor-liquid-liquid equilibrium (VLLE) with creation-order roles phaseArray[0] = SRK gas, phaseArray[1] = Pitzer aqueous and phaseArray[2] = SRK oil. Enable the dedicated hybrid strategy by calling setMultiPhaseCheck(true) before running the flash. Phase disappearance only changes the active mapping; repeated flashes, cloning and serialization retain the role objects. Systems initialized through chemicalReactionInit() alternate fixed-role phase equilibrium with chemical equilibrium in the Pitzer aqueous phase, enabling reactive gas-aqueous and gas-oil-aqueous scale-potential calculations.

The hybrid TP strategy supports fluid phases only. Incipient hydrate temperature, pressure and equilibrium curves are available through ThermodynamicOperations using a Pitzer-consistent liquid-water reference and a bounded outer search. This does not compute hydrate amounts. Solid and wax checks are rejected explicitly when the hybrid TP strategy is active.

    • useLegacyPitzerParameters

      public void useLegacyPitzerParameters()
      Selects legacy Pitzer parameter loading for compatibility with historical calculations.

      The default is to use the bundled PHREEQC catalog whenever it contains every interaction required by the active aqueous topology. Call this method before the first activity or property evaluation only when reproducing a legacy result is required.

    • refreshDefaultPitzerParameterSelection

      public boolean refreshDefaultPitzerParameterSelection()
      Refreshes catalog-first parameter selection after the active aqueous topology changes.

      Component identities can be added after an earlier property evaluation selected the legacy fallback for a water-only topology. This method re-runs the complete catalog audit for the now-active species without changing an explicit useLegacyPitzerParameters() selection. Missing catalog rows leave the existing coherent fallback untouched.

      Returns:
      true when the complete PHREEQC catalog was applied to the active topology

    • getPitzerParameterQualification

      public PitzerParameterQualification getPitzerParameterQualification()
      Returns scientific qualification metadata for the selected Pitzer parameter dataset.

      Calling this method completes lazy dataset selection and the active ionic-topology coverage audit. It does not run a flash or enter ordinary property kernels.

      Returns:
      immutable qualification metadata for the selected dataset identity

    • requireCompletePitzerDatasetQualification

      public PitzerParameterQualification requireCompletePitzerDatasetQualification()
      Requires complete interaction coverage and complete scientific qualification of the named Pitzer dataset.

      This is an explicit publication gate. A broad dataset with only partially validated subsystems is rejected even when it covers the active topology. A successful result still requires the caller to check the appropriate subsystem-specific temperature and molality range helper. This legacy gate does not select an observable; use requirePitzerDatasetValidationFor(ValidationTarget) before publishing a property-specific calculation.

      Returns:
      immutable qualification metadata for the accepted dataset
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when interaction coverage is incomplete or the complete dataset is not validated

    • requirePitzerDatasetValidationFor

      public PitzerParameterQualification requirePitzerDatasetValidationFor(PitzerParameterQualification.ValidationTarget target)
      Requires complete interaction coverage and independent qualification for one scientific target.

      This explicit publication gate does not run a flash and does not check whether the current temperature, pressure, or composition lies inside the evidence envelope. Callers must also use the applicable dataset-specific range helper in PitzerParameterDatasets.

      Parameters:
      target - requested property or equilibrium target
      Returns:
      immutable qualification metadata for the accepted dataset and target
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when target is null
      IllegalStateException - when coverage is incomplete or the target lacks independent qualification

    • applyPhreeqcCo2SodiumSulfateParameters

      public void applyPhreeqcCo2SodiumSulfateParameters()
      Applies the qualified public-domain PHREEQC CO2-Na2SO4 parameter subset to this system's Pitzer aqueous role.

      The dataset is intentionally fail-closed: additional active species require explicit companion interactions. See PitzerParameterDatasets.applyPhreeqcCo2SodiumSulfate(PhasePitzer) for source identity and validation scope.

    • applyPhreeqcSodiumPotassiumChlorideParameters

      public void applyPhreeqcSodiumPotassiumChlorideParameters()
      Applies the qualified public-domain PHREEQC Na-K-Cl parameter subset to this system's Pitzer aqueous role.

      The dataset contains both binary families and their same-sign and ternary mixed-ion companions. It is intentionally fail-closed if another active ionic or neutral species lacks a qualified interaction. See PitzerParameterDatasets.applyPhreeqcSodiumPotassiumChloride(PhasePitzer) for source identity and validation scope.

    • applyCompletePhreeqcPitzerCatalogParameters

      public void applyCompletePhreeqcPitzerCatalogParameters()
      Applies the complete explicit PHREEQC Pitzer subset required by this system's active aqueous species.

      The bundled source catalog is broad, but activation remains fail-closed: every required binary, same-sign, ternary, and neutral interaction for the active aqueous topology must exist explicitly. Gas and oil remain on their EOS role phases and do not invoke the catalog.

    • clone

      public SystemPitzer clone()
      Creates an independently mutable copy of this thermodynamic system.

      Phase, component, and initialized chemical-reaction state in the returned system are owned by the copy. Changing or solving a reactive clone must therefore not mutate the source system.
